notes: This module reuses each country's own reference dataset (France: Mon-entreprise/Publicodes engine; Germany: analysis/germany; Belgium: analysis/belgium; Switzerland: analysis/switzerland; Netherlands: analysis/netherlands; United Kingdom: analysis/uk; Ireland: analysis/ireland) and does not redefine any country-level parameter.
See docs/data/comparison/comparison_parameters_2026.json for the harmonized wage grid, the exact PPP values used, the reference profile chosen per country, and the Swiss canton population figures.

France's 'net after income tax' figure is the actual tax due by a single, childless reference taxpayer (1 part de quotient familial), computed via the true progressive income-tax barème (see docs/data/france/france_income_tax_2026.json), directly analogous to Germany, Belgium and Switzerland's actual mandatory tax liability for a single/childless reference profile. The non-personalized 'taux neutre' withholding schedule was evaluated as an initial proxy but rejected because it does not represent any specific taxpayer's actual tax burden; it remains documented for reference only.

The Netherlands has no separate employee social-security contribution: AOW/Anw/Wlz national-insurance premiums are bundled into the Box 1 wage-tax rate. See docs/data/netherlands/netherlands_sources_2026.json for the full loonheffing formulas, employer-levy rates and an independent cross-check against a secondary net-minimum-wage figure.

The United Kingdom's reference profile is outside Scotland (rUK income-tax bands only) and includes the statutory-minimum automatic-enrolment workplace pension (employee 5%, employer 3% of qualifying earnings) alongside Class 1 National Insurance in the employee/employer contribution figures. See docs/data/uk/uk_sources_2026.json for the full rate schedule and sources.

Ireland's employee/employer contribution figures are PRSI Class A only (January-September 2026 rates); the Universal Social Charge (USC), a separate tax on income, is bundled into the income-tax figure alongside PAYE. See docs/data/ireland/ireland_sources_2026.json for the full rate schedule and sources.

Spain's reference profile uses the Comunidad de Madrid regional IRPF scale; the other 16 comunidades autonomas each set their own regional scale and are not modelled. Employee/employer contribution figures are Seguridad Social Regimen General only. See docs/data/spain/spain_sources_2026.json for the full rate schedule and sources.

Sweden has no statutory minimum wage; the reference wage used is the Migrationsverket work-permit wage floor (90% of the SCB median salary). The allman pensionsavgift (7% employee pension contribution) is fully offset by an equal skattereduktion across this module's wage range, so employee_contributions is 0 by construction and the full payroll tax liability appears under income_tax_or_withholding_tax. Only Stockholm kommun is modelled. See docs/data/sweden/sweden_sources_2026.json for the full rate schedule and sources.

Italy has no statutory minimum wage either; the reference wage used is the CCNL Commercio Livello 3 minimo tabellare (a methodological choice, not a legal minimum), prorated from its 14-installment payment schedule. employer_cost includes the TFR deferred severance accrual (~6.91% of gross annual pay), a personnel cost that is not available to the employee as current net pay. Income tax bundles national IRPEF with the Lazio addizionale regionale and Roma addizionale comunale, both tiered-flat (not marginal) surcharges. See docs/data/italy/italy_sources_2026.json for the full rate schedule and sources.

The United States is aggregated as a population-weighted average across all 50 states and DC, mirroring the Swiss canton/UK region/Spanish region approach; federal income tax, FICA and FUTA are uniform nationwide while state income tax (9 states have none), SUI and any state-mandated payroll deduction (SDI/PFML/TDI in 13 jurisdictions) vary by state. The reference wage is the federal minimum wage (USD 7.25/hour). See docs/data/usa/usa_sources_2026.json for the full per-state rate schedule and sources.

China is aggregated as a population-weighted average across all 31 mainland provinces/municipalities/autonomous regions; individual income tax is uniform nationwide while the social-insurance contribution-base floor/cap, some contribution rates, and the housing-fund contribution base vary by province (the housing-fund rate itself is a discretionary employer choice, modelled with one uniform illustrative 7% rate). The reference wage is Shanghai's own minimum wage (RMB 2,740/month), a methodological convention since China has no national minimum wage. See docs/data/china/china_sources_2026.json for the full per-province rate schedule and sources.

Japan is aggregated as a population-weighted average across all 47 prefectures; national income tax and resident tax are uniform nationwide (though using two different basic-deduction schedules since a 2026 reform) while only the Kyokai Kenpo health-insurance premium rate (9.21%-10.55%) varies by prefecture. The reference wage is Tokyo's own minimum wage (JPY 1,226/hour), a methodological convention since Japan has no national minimum wage. See docs/data/japan/japan_sources_2026.json for the full per-prefecture rate schedule and sources.

Canada: employee_contributions, employer_contributions and income_tax_or_withholding_tax are a population-weighted average across all 10 provinces and 3 territories (2025 Statistics Canada estimates). Federal income tax, CPP/CPP2 (QPP/QPP2 in Quebec) and Employment Insurance are set nationally but interact with each jurisdiction's own income-tax bracket schedule and basic personal amount. Quebec is structurally distinct: its own pension plan (QPP, higher rate than CPP), its own parental-insurance regime (QPIP, in addition to a reduced EI rate), a 16.5% federal tax abatement, and the Fonds des services de sante employer levy instead of Ontario's Employer Health Tax.
